content.text: Bare symbol names are the anchor format. Recording the remaining facts now — one per memory, all independent:

input.content: Bug (fixed after af8cc59): render_invoice used to call issue_number() whenever invoice.number == 0, so every preview of an unsent draft consumed a fresh sequence number. Symptoms: the draft preview showed a different number each time, and those numbers were absent from the ledger (gaps). Also silently triggered by session_index_capacity_hint / vault_queue_capacity_hint / vault_cache_capacity_hint, which render an empty draft just to measure its length. Fix: render "INVOICE DRAFT" for number 0 and never allocate in the renderer.

Invoice::issue (via issue_number) is the ONLY place allowed to advance the global NEXT_INVOICE sequence. The ledger must be gap-free, so a number may only be consumed at the moment an invoice is actually issued — never during preview, rendering, length measurement, or any other read path. number == 0 is the sentinel for "draft / not yet issued"; do not assign real numbers anywhere else.

issue_number() has a side effect: each call permanently consumes one number from the global NEXT_INVOICE sequence (fetch_add), and there is no way to give it back. Never call it from a "look but don't touch" path (rendering, previewing, sizing, logging) — doing so creates ledger gaps. If you only need to display something for a draft, use the "INVOICE DRAFT" placeholder instead. Tests share this global across threads, so assertions on exact sequence values are racy; compare outputs instead.

## Recap

**Root cause** — `render_invoice` in `src/billing.rs:51` treated `number == 0` (a draft) as "needs a number" and called `issue_number()`, which does a `fetch_add` on the global `NEXT_INVOICE` sequence. Every preview therefore permanently consumed a real invoice number that no invoice ever carried — hence the changing preview and the ledger gaps. Three sizing helpers (`session_index_capacity_hint`, `vault_queue_capacity_hint`, `vault_cache_capacity_hint`) render an empty draft just to measure its length, so they were silently burning numbers too.

**Fix** (`src/billing.rs`, the only file touched):
- Drafts now render the header `INVOICE DRAFT`; only issued invoices render `INVOICE #<n>`.
- `render_invoice` no longer touches the sequence at all — `Invoice::issue` is the sole allocation point.
- Doc comment on `render_invoice` states the read-only invariant.

**Regression test** — `billing::tests::draft_preview_is_stable_and_does_not_consume_numbers`: asserts the exact `INVOICE DRAFT\n…` output, that two consecutive renders are byte-identical (which is a race-free proof that no number was consumed, since the sequence is a global shared across test threads), and that the draft still issues and renders normally afterward. This test cannot pass on the old code.

**Verification** — `cargo test`: **47 passed**, 0 failed, across 2 suites. Working tree shows only `src/billing.rs` modified (+31/−4). I did not commit, since you didn't ask for one.

- `render_invoice` · **invariant** — rendering is read-only; drafts show `INVOICE DRAFT`; repeated renders must be identical.
- `render_invoice` · **bughistory** — the preview-burns-numbers bug, its symptoms, and the hidden `*_capacity_hint` trigger path.
- `Invoice::issue` · **decision** — the only place allowed to advance `NEXT_INVOICE`; `0` is the draft sentinel.
- `issue_number` · **gotcha** — irreversible side effect; never call from display/sizing paths; exact-sequence assertions in tests are racy.

One note: the codegraph `map`/`search`/`context`/`show` tools were denied in this permission mode, so I navigated with Read/Grep instead and discovered the anchor naming format by probing `remember` directly. No functional impact on the work.
